blocks.text: Santiago de Chile to San Pedro de Atacama

After breakfast, transfer to the airport and fly to Calama. On arrival, transfer to San Pedro de Atacama.

In the afternoon, visit the Valley of the Moon. A few kilometres from San Pedro, it lies among the rocks and unusual geological formations of the Cordillera de la Sal, within Los Flamencos National Reserve.

The route crosses landscapes often compared to the surface of the Moon. Different viewpoints look out over the Andes and their volcanoes. At sunset, the desert turns gold and red.

Stargazing is planned for after sunset. The Atacama is known for its exceptionally clear skies and is regarded as one of the best regions for astronomical observations.

The changing light and colours shape the afternoon. While the sun is still high, the jagged ridges of the Cordillera de la Sal and the volcanoes on the horizon stand out. Towards evening, the rocks and sand turn gold and red. After dark, attention shifts from the landscape to the stars above the desert.
Santiago high-rises below snow-covered Andean peaks in Chile
Santiago: glass towers against snow-covered mountains
San Pedro de Atacama to Uyuni

After breakfast, set out across the high-altitude desert towards Uyuni.

The first part of the route takes you to Laguna Verde at the foot of Licancabur Volcano. Then see the Dalí Desert, with its wind-shaped rock formations.

The next stop is Polques, where you can bathe in the hot springs. The route then passes through Sol de Mañana, an area of fumaroles and geysers with visible volcanic activity.

Before continuing to the hotel, see the Stone Tree, one of the region’s best-known rock formations, and Laguna Colorada. The lagoon is known for the colour of its water and provides a habitat and breeding ground for flamingos.

Overnight at an expedition-style hotel.

This high-altitude day is devoted almost entirely to natural landmarks. Laguna Verde, Licancabur Volcano, the Dalí Desert and the Polques Hot Springs follow one another as you head towards Bolivia. At Sol de Mañana, you can see active fumaroles and geysers. Laguna Colorada is a highlight of the route for its unusually coloured water and flamingo colonies.
